**Profitability trend for Snowflake Inc. (CIK 1640147), fiscal years ended January 31, FY2019–FY2025**

Snowflake grew revenue very rapidly but remained loss-making on every reported profitability measure throughout the period; losses widened in absolute dollars even as gross margin improved. All figures are consolidated, USD, annual (fiscal_period = FY, end_date = Jan 31), from the latest applicable 10-K disclosures (FY2024: accession 0001640147-24-000101; FY2025: 0001640147-25-000052).

**Disclosed annual values (USD):**

| FY (end Jan 31) | Revenue | Gross profit | Operating income (loss) | Net loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 96,666,000 | 44,913,000 | (185,465,000) | (178,028,000) |
| 2020 | 264,748,000 | 148,191,000 | (358,088,000) | (348,535,000) |
| 2021 | 592,049,000 | 349,461,000 | (543,937,000) | (539,102,000) |
| 2022 | 1,219,327,000 | 760,894,000 | (715,036,000) | (679,948,000) |
| 2023 | 2,065,659,000 | 1,348,119,000 | (842,267,000) | (796,705,000) |
| 2024 | 2,806,489,000 | 1,907,931,000 | (1,094,773,000) | (836,097,000) |
| 2025 | 3,626,396,000 | 2,411,723,000 | (1,456,010,000) | (1,285,640,000) |

Source fact IDs (latest disclosure): revenue 2509651/2509654/2509663/2509676/2509689/2509702/2509712; gross profit 2506701/2506704/2506713/2506726/2506739/2506752/2506762; operating income 2507965/2507968/2507977/2507990/2508003/2508016/2508026; net income 2507770/2507773/2507782/2507795/2507808/2507821/2507831. Repeated comparative disclosures across 10-Ks were identical (no revisions found), so no double counting.

**Derived margins (calculated, not disclosed):**
- Gross margin: 46.5% (FY2019) → 56.0% (FY2020); the remaining years' ratios could not be computed because the calculation tool budget was exhausted. Using the disclosed values above, gross margin is approximately 59.0% (FY2021), 62.4% (FY2022), 65.3% (FY2023), 68.0% (FY2024) and 66.5% (FY2025) — these later figures are my arithmetic from the table, not tool-verified.
- Operating margin: negative in all years, roughly −192% (FY2019), −135% (FY2020), −92% (FY2021), −59% (FY2022), −41% (FY2023), −39% (FY2024), −40% (FY2025) — i.e., operating losses shrank sharply as a share of revenue but the dollar loss grew every year.
- Net margin: negative throughout, roughly −184% (FY2019) narrowing to about −35% (FY2025), with the FY2025 net loss (−$1.29B) larger than the operating loss because of a tax expense (pretax loss −$1,285,099,000 vs. net loss −$1,285,640,000; operating loss −$1,456,010,000).

**Drivers visible in the data:** operating expense growth outpaced revenue growth in dollar terms — R&D rose from $68.7M (FY2019) to $1,783.4M (FY2025), sales & marketing from $1,106.5M (FY2023) to $1,672.1M (FY2025), and G&A from $36.1M to $412.3M — consistent with heavy investment in growth rather than a profitability deterioration in gross terms.

**Limitations:** The question does not specify a period, so I used the full annual series available (FY2019–FY2025). Quarterly figures exist in the database but are not comparable to annual flows and were not used. Only the FY2019 and FY2020 gross-margin ratios were tool-verified; later margin percentages are arithmetic on disclosed values and should be treated as derived. No adjusted/non-GAAP profitability measures were analyzed.
